summary: A member can release old envelope payloads locally, and no peer or backup then needs them: once an envelope is 14 days old, alone in its batch, holds only valid records, carries no fleet, principal, pairing, daemon.started or message.sent claim, is not its writer's newest, has its writer's envelope signature by a key membership admits, and every claim of it carries its writer's signature by such a key, its payload, envelope signatures, hold and claim records are deleted and its identity stays in released_envelopes with that envelope signature. A peer that lists the capability signed-claims-v1 is sent such an envelope's claims as signed claims and admits them after checking every signature, the batch header and each claim id; a backup carries them the same way. Readers, inventories and digests do not change. The pass ships switched off (ENVELOPE_RELEASE)

replay.detail: No replay. Readers that find a claim's envelope by its batch (admission, the record view, the self-writer, writer and pairing signer checks, sealing, record repairs and the local trim capture and delete) read stored and released envelopes alike. For a released envelope the signer checks accept the claim's own writer signature (claim_member_signatures) by the key membership admits for that writer and sequence; the envelope signature path is unchanged for stored envelopes. Readers of payloads (export, backup, wire archive, signature migration and backfill, rename proofs) skip released envelopes. The scoped capture's record counts and late-claim checks seek their own indexes instead of running the record view in full for each claim and writer. A received signed envelope is admitted as envelope admission stores valid claims (positions, principal signatures, blobs, writer signatures), then projected with the backlog.

schema.detail: New table released_envelopes (identity, previous hash, accepted time, batch, original rowid, release time, the writer's envelope key and signature; indexes on batch_id and a unique one on original_rowid) and view envelope_rows (stored and released envelopes, by row_id). An identity received as released takes an original rowid below zero, so every capture counts it as sealed. The view replica_record_rows gains a branch for released envelopes and is replaced on open when its definition differs. The inventory trigger replica_envelopes_inventory_DELETE_v2 is replaced by _v3, which also leaves a released envelope's deletion uncounted; saved-inventory triggers count an identity received as released and a released row's deletion. New meta key envelope_release_cursor. Backup archives that hold signed envelopes are version 7 (VERSION_WITH_SIGNED_CLAIMS); an archive with none keeps an earlier version. No storage version change; nothing is written to the new table while the pass is off.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule or fleet coordination change. A local cut drops a released envelope's claims as it would a stored one's, and its tombstone then stands for the identity.

compatibility.detail: Inventories list an optional capabilities field; this build lists signed-claims-v1, and older peers neither send nor read it. An exchange carries an optional signed_envelopes list, sent only to a peer that lists signed-claims-v1: each released envelope's identity with its writer's envelope signature, its batch header, and each claim with its position, writer signature, principal signature and the blobs it names. The receiver admits one only when the envelope signature and every claim signature verify by a key membership admits for that writer and sequence (Legacy and Fenced refuse; a writer membership does not key yet waits for a later exchange), the batch header recomputes its id, each claim id is its content's hash and the runtime classifies it valid, and each blob is its hash; it then lists the identity as released too and never asks again. Refused ones are counted (refused_signed_envelopes in the replication status). A peer without the capability gets every envelope this member still holds but none it released; how many it lacks is in the replication status (unservable_released, by peer) and logged once per peer. A build before version 7 refuses an archive that holds signed envelopes; archives up to version 6 restore as before.

downtime.detail: No startup work beyond creating the table, view and replaced trigger and view in the opening transaction. When a later release switches the pass on, it reads envelopes in rowid order, at most 512 and 10 ms of writer work a page, then gives the freed pages back 128 at a time.

recovery.detail: Rollback to the previous release is supported while the pass is off: released_envelopes is empty, no signed envelope is sent or received, backups stay at version 6 or below, the previous release keeps this build's replica_record_rows definition (it creates the view only when missing), which reads the same rows while nothing is released, and it recreates replica_envelopes_inventory_DELETE_v2 beside _v3, so a deletion both count moves the inventory generation twice, which only rebuilds a snapshot that was rebuilt anyway. Once a later release has released envelopes or received signed ones, the previous release would not find their claims admitted or their records, and refuses version 7 archives; that release's note states the floor.
